metadata.course: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: An introductory Earth and space science course: Earth's place in the universe, plate tectonics and Earth's structure, weather and climate, and Earth's resources and human impact.

concepts.title: Air masses and fronts
concepts.summary: Weather changes sharply at a front because two air masses with different properties meet.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Air pressure, wind and global circulation
concepts.summary: Uneven heating creates pressure differences, and rotation deflects the resulting flow.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Climate versus weather
concepts.summary: Weather is the state of the atmosphere now; climate is the statistics of that state over decades.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Clouds, humidity and precipitation
concepts.summary: Air cools as it rises, water vapour condenses onto nuclei, and droplets grow until they fall.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Continental drift and the evidence for it
concepts.summary: Matching coastlines, fossils and rock sequences were explained only once the continents were allowed to move.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Earthquakes and their measurement
concepts.summary: Magnitude measures energy released while intensity measures the effect at a place, so they differ for one event.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Energy balance and the greenhouse effect
concepts.summary: Incoming solar radiation must be balanced by outgoing radiation, and greenhouse gases shift where that balance sits.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Energy resources and their trade-offs
concepts.summary: Every generation source has a different mix of cost, reliability, land use and emissions.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Evidence for recent climate change
concepts.summary: Temperature records, ice cores, sea level and phenology are independent lines that agree.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Evidence from seismic waves
concepts.summary: Seismic waves bend and stop at boundaries, which is how the interior was mapped without ever seeing it.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Feedback loops in the climate system
concepts.summary: Positive feedbacks amplify a change and negative feedbacks damp it, and ice albedo is a strong positive one.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Formation of the solar system
concepts.summary: A collapsing cloud of gas and dust flattened into a disc, and the Sun ignited at its centre.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Galaxies and the expanding universe
concepts.summary: Distant galaxies recede faster, which is the observation that the universe is expanding.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Glaciers and glacial landforms
concepts.summary: Ice erodes differently from water, leaving characteristic U-shaped valleys and deposited moraine.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Groundwater and aquifers
concepts.summary: Water stored in permeable rock moves slowly, and withdrawing it faster than recharge lowers the water table.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Impacts and adaptation
concepts.summary: Impacts differ by region and by capacity to adapt, so the same warming is not the same experience.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Layers of the Earth
concepts.summary: Crust, mantle, outer core and inner core are distinguished by composition and by mechanical behaviour.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Mineral and water resource distribution
concepts.summary: Resources are unevenly distributed, which makes supply a geopolitical as well as a geological question.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Minerals and their identification
concepts.summary: Hardness, cleavage, lustre and streak identify a mineral more reliably than colour.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Mitigation and energy transition
concepts.summary: Mitigation reduces the cause rather than managing the effect, and it requires replacing the energy source.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Moon phases, eclipses and tides
concepts.summary: Phases, eclipses and tides are all consequences of relative position and gravity, not of the Moon changing shape.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Mountain building and deformation
concepts.summary: Folding and faulting are the visible result of crustal stress exceeding what rock can bear.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Natural climate drivers
concepts.summary: Orbital cycles, volcanic activity and solar variation all changed climate before human influence.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Natural hazards and risk reduction
concepts.summary: Risk combines hazard, exposure and vulnerability, so reducing any one of the three reduces risk.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Orbital motion and seasons
concepts.summary: Seasons come from the tilt of Earth's axis, not from its changing distance from the Sun.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Plate boundaries and their hazards
concepts.summary: Divergent, convergent and transform boundaries each produce a characteristic set of hazards.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Relative and absolute dating
concepts.summary: Superposition gives order while radiometric decay gives age, and together they give a timeline.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Renewable and non-renewable resources
concepts.summary: The distinction is about the rate of replenishment relative to the rate of use.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: River processes and landforms
concepts.summary: A river erodes, transports and deposits along its course, building different landforms at each stage.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Seafloor spreading
concepts.summary: Magnetic stripes recorded symmetrically either side of a ridge are direct evidence that new crust forms there.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Soil formation and conservation
concepts.summary: Soil forms over long periods from parent rock and organic matter, and erodes far faster than it forms.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Structure and composition of the atmosphere
concepts.summary: Temperature changes direction at layer boundaries, and each layer has a different role.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Sustainable use and carrying capacity
concepts.summary: Use is sustainable only while it stays within the rate at which the system can renew itself.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Terrestrial and gas giant planets
concepts.summary: Distance from the Sun during formation decided whether a planet kept a thick volatile envelope or not.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: The fossil record and geological time
concepts.summary: The geological timescale was assembled from fossil succession before any radiometric date existed.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: The life cycle of stars
concepts.summary: A star's mass decides its whole history, including whether it ends as a white dwarf, neutron star or black hole.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: The rock cycle
concepts.summary: Igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are three states of the same material under different conditions.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: The scale of the universe
concepts.summary: Astronomical distances are so large that a scaled model almost always misleads unless it is built carefully.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: The Sun and stellar processes
concepts.summary: Stars fuse light nuclei into heavier ones, releasing the energy that drives everything around them.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: The water cycle
concepts.summary: Water moves between ocean, atmosphere and land, and the cycle is powered by the Sun.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Volcanoes and magma
concepts.summary: Magma viscosity, set by silica content, decides whether an eruption is gentle or explosive.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Waste, recycling and circular economy
concepts.summary: Designing for reuse changes the material flow at the design stage rather than after disposal.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Weather prediction and forecasting
concepts.summary: Forecasts come from numerical models, and their skill decays with lead time in a way that can be estimated.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos

concepts.title: Weathering and erosion
concepts.summary: Weathering breaks rock in place while erosion transports the pieces, and they are different processes.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science — Systems, Climate and the Cosmos
